title: The Third Perfection and the Testing of the Word
english: They say they desired salvation: 'O God, you tested us, you burned us like silver is burned; you brought us into a snare, you set tribulations before us'—or 'into our midst'; for it is also carried in many manuscripts—'you brought up men upon our necks, we passed through fire and water, and you brought us out into refreshment.'

Similarly in Isaiah, regarding the one who helps and does good, it says: 'Do not fear, for I am with you; and if you pass through water, rivers shall not overwhelm you; and if you walk through fire, flame shall not burn you, for I am with you' (Isa 43:2). When, then, does anyone pass through fire and remain unharmed, unless he has possessed the voice of God, concerning which it was said: 'The voice of the Lord breaking a flaming fire' (Ps 29:7)? Just as the people crossed the Red Sea with the holy rod without any loss, as the flame of the fire was broken and divided, so the crossing proceeds without being consumed by the flame.

What remained of the third in the Hebrew plurality, the two parts having been destroyed and having ceased, was tested according to the intellect, both gold and silver, passing through fire. Similarly it is carried in Wisdom: 'Just as gold and silver are tested in a furnace, so are chosen hearts before God' (Wis 2:5). The same thought is held by what the apostle Peter writes in his epistle, exhorting to bear tribulations bravely and magnanimously, especially those concerning faith.

And his word has it thus: 'In which rejoice, though you may sometimes be grieved in various trials, so that the testing of your faith may be found more precious than gold being tested by fire; for it shall be found unto praise and glory' (1 Pet 1:6-7). In agreement, James also addresses the disciples of the Gospel: 'Count it all joy, beloved brothers, when you fall into various trials, knowing that the testing of you works patience; and let patience have a perfect work, so that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing' (Jas 1:2-4). For thus, having been prepared, those to whom the word is addressed, having been burned like silver according to the word and having been tested like gold according to their own intellect, shall have God listening, calling upon His name, as He benefits them as a people.

To turn from the benefactor to their own God. The matter laid before is being tortured and is otherwise clear. In the Church of Christ, there are some practicing superstition and others Judaizing among them, even as they also sincerely fear God, in whom the apostles, being said to speak wisdom, have all progressed as far as to reach 'a perfect man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of the knowledge of the Son of God' (Eph 4:13).

The two destroying parts will be cut away, so that they may no longer practice superstition or Judaize according to the ways of the Ebionites. For when this has been endured, only the perfect of the Church will remain in it, so that they indeed may be made 'the people of God' (1 Pet 2:10), and He himself may be confessed as 'their God' (Ex 21:6).

Understand precisely even if a third theory may be said regarding the things set forth. Each of the virtues lies in the middle of two evils, excess and deficiency: courage and temperance, the one being the middle of rashness and cowardice, the other of intemperance and foolishness, just as piety has excess in superstition and deficiency in impiety. Similarly, the free man, being social and giving, has the best middle, of which profligacy is excess and stinginess is deficiency.

And since of those sinning, some by excesses—doing rashness, superstition, and profligacy—and others by deficiencies—doing impiety, cowardice, and stinginess—these two ranks and parts must necessarily be destroyed and cut away having fallen under punishment, the third being perfected, being refined and tested like silver and gold, which is the word and the mind, in order to be tested and perfected according to the following virtues, having surpassed the deficiencies and excesses.

It is said from property and another scientific thought thus: 'those bearing the image of the swine', partaking of a material disposition, become unclean, approaching that which is called an indefinite duality toward some. And according to the Scripture, indeed, the unclean of the animals are taken two by two, while the clean are brought into the ark seven by seven, belonging to the incorruptible virgin week (Gen 7:2). And since those bearing the image of the swine are two, the quality of these is also cut away and destroyed, so that the third may be revealed as tested 'of those bearing the image of...'

title: The Desolation of Women and Property
english: The wise man applies each word of the text to each of the fulfillments. It is possible to understand that the third remains in that day on which these things previously spoken shall occur.

Behold, days are coming of the Lord, and your dogs shall be divided in you (Zach. 14:1-2). And I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem for war, and the city shall be captured, and the houses shall be plundered, and the women shall be violated, and half the city shall go out in captivity, but the remnant of my people shall not be destroyed from the city (Zach. 14:2). He says 'Days of the Lord' according to how the burdensome and punishing things come upon the guilty, and there are many witnesses to this by understanding. And in Isaiah, indeed, the time of God's punishments is called a day thus: 'A day of the Lord comes, unyielding, in fury and wrath, to lay the whole inhabited world waste and to destroy the sinners from it' (Isa. 9:3).

Since, therefore, he announces fearsome things shall be to those against whom God is indignant because of their grasping impiety and other sins, it is fitting he says there shall be days of the Lord in which there will be most pitiful wickedness toward Jerusalem and its citizens. For why is it so pitiful and unyielding, that the dogs which the coming enemies took, to be divided in its midst because of much existing weakness? But this does not always happen; for there is a time when those who plundered, far from the city, rather the land, having carried off the spoils, are divided, fearing that they might be prevented from dividing them in the city by those who have captured breathing.

After the word having spoken: 'Behold, days are coming of the Lord, and your dogs shall be divided in your midst' (Zach. 14:2), the Lord immediately says to gather against them all the nations for war, just as a day becomes one of mobilization, of the armies of the gathered nations toward the waging of war against Jerusalem. For toward it is announced the dividing of its dogs in it, and even the houses of the inhabitants shall be plundered, and their women shall be violated. For what manner of way is painful and extremely unyielding is the dividing of those who grasped, in the sight of the citizens, especially when not only the common and...

Not only public treasures but also those of each person, as their houses are being plundered; moreover, regarding all these things, it is both sorrowful and heavy to be shamefully violated, seeing those who live together being unable to prevent the lawless act after much weakness has taken hold, just as half of the city itself has been torn away outside its own town, seeing nothing of this kind among those being guarded by the right hand of God. These are the ones fulfilling the third [part], it having been said that they shall be saved after the two parts have been destroyed and left behind.

5.26 Such a harsh providence the divine word threatens also in Isaiah; and thus the prophetic speech has: 'Those who are gathered together,' turned toward one another, 'shall fall by the sword; and your children shall be thrown down before you, and your houses shall be plundered, and your women shall be taken' (Isa 5:17).

5.27 The excess is shown in the women suffering violence from tyrannizing enemies in addition to the men living with them, and from what was said to the worthless priest Amaziah by the prophet Amos, seeing sharply: 'Your wife in the city shall commit fornication, and your land shall be measured with a cord' (Amos 8:2). Both the threatened things are painful and cause agony to those living together, seeing the cohabitants inside the city and not outside it, being corrupted in their lawful marital rights by the most savage enemies, and their own land being measured with a cord, while the owners are present and are not strong enough to prevent the violence.

5.28 It happened... such things happened many times to those dwelling in Jerusalem and in Judah, the Jews being taken by the nations because of the impiety they received, having killed the Lord. 'For having watched, and having studied the emptiness and futility of the peoples, and having brought forward the kings and the rulers, having been gathered together against the Lord and against His Christ, God incited them and stirred them up, speaking in wrath against them and in His own anger unsettling them,' just as the Apostle wrote the same concerning those killing the Lord and the prophets and driving out the apostles: 'The wrath has come upon them to its end' (Rom 11:22).

title: The Divine Descent and Motion
english: Joseph, his name, wrote truly and with precision the misfortunes, famines, and other much more distressing evils that were coming upon the nation, which the beauty-loving reader, rejoicing in reading, is inclined to see toward a love of learning and a fear of not suffering the same.

He says [that they are] not being driven out of the city by the cruel tyrants, whom God tests in fire as silver and gold are tested, in order that their vainglory and condemnation might be known. [Zechariah 14:3-4: The Lord will arise and line up against those nations as on a day of battle. And his feet shall stand on the Mount of Olives that is before Jerusalem on the east; and the Mount of Olives shall be split in two, half of it toward the east and half toward the sea, a very great chaos.]

God, being incorporeal, rather exceeding all spiritual substance, is without reception of those things pertaining to bodies—colors, forms, and magnitudes—I say, whence he is invisible. For every visible substance must exist under forms, magnitudes, colors, and their adjacents, but God is invisible, as many words of the Scriptures testify, being a spiritual substance, nor does he move transitionally, nor does the whole exist in a place.

It is sufficient to receive the testimony having such [characteristics]: 'Who is the image of the invisible God' [Colossians 1:15], and again: 'To the King of the ages, the incorruptible invisible God' [1 Timothy 6:16]. The apostolic words and the evangelical ones declare the same: she [the Scripture] having thus: 'No one has seen God at any time; the only-begotten God who is in the bosom of the Father has made him known' [John 1:18], and again: 'Not that anyone has seen God, except the one who is from the Father' [John 6:46].

Since, therefore, these things are rightly said and thought concerning God, the more bodily things concerning him announced economically in the divine Scriptures must be understood spiritually and appropriately. For the manner of him being said in the prophet: 'I have not changed' [Malachi 3:6], and of the theologians saying similarly, the one hymnographer to the one being glorified saying: 'But you are the same,' and: 'But you remain,' and of Jacob writing about the...

Suffering and unchangeable. 'Every good gift and every perfect gift comes down from above from the Father of lights, with whom there is no change or shadow of turning' (James 1:17). And just as we grasp and understand the words concerning his repentance and his wrath and those of the neighbors, so, since he is incorporeal, we receive the words concerning ascending and descending, and going out and coming in, in harmony with the thought concerning him.

Therefore, in the present prophecy where it is written: 'The Lord will go forth' (Zephaniah 1:15), we do not imagine a changing motion; for such motions belong to bodies. 5.36 Since, therefore, it does not fit to confess these things concerning an invisible essence, yet they are carried in the divinely inspired oracles, it is necessary to oversee how they must be understood piously. 5.37 Being a fountain of goodness and 'full of grace and truth' (John 1:14), the cause of all things, descending in sympathy with those being managed by him, becomes outside himself as if he were among them. For the Lord and our Savior says in the Gospels concerning himself: 'I went out from God and I have come; for I did not come from myself, but he sent me' (John 16:28). With the same thought the prophet Habakkuk spoke toward him: 'You went out for the salvation of your people, to save your anointed ones' (Habakkuk 3:3). 5.38 And just as he goes out and comes to those being saved, so much more when he is wroth or wars. For it is written concerning Michael: 'Behold, the Lord goes forth from his house, and he shall be among us for a witness and shall descend' (Jude 1:9), and in Isaiah: 'The Lord of powers will go forth and will crush war, and he will arouse zeal and will cry out against his enemies with strength' (Isaiah 63:3). 5.39 Considering these things in a God-befitting manner, God is said to go out 'upon the nations, that he may array himself against them as in a day of war' (Zephaniah 1:15) when 'his feet shall stand upon the Mount of Olives toward the east' (Zechariah 14:4); for where must his feet stand, since he is no longer moving in indignation, according to what was already previously said: 'And the Lord will sound the trumpet and will go forth in the threat of his wrath' (Zephaniah 1:16)?
